newsitem.title: TAIWAN: TAIWAN MONEY RATES END DOWN ON FUND INJECTION.
newsitem.headline: TAIWAN MONEY RATES END DOWN ON FUND INJECTION.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates closed sharply lower on Wednesday following the central bank's persistent fund injections into the banking system, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate dropped sharply to close at 8.601 percent against Tuesday's 9.789 end -- but still well above the central bank's previously declared 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper fell one percentage point to 7.75-8.00 percent against 8.75-9.00.
The central bank on Wednesday morning injected T$27.145 billion worth of funds into the banking system through open market operation following days of such injections to alleviate tight liquidity.
It injected T$35 billion worth of funds on Tuesday.
Dealers expected the money rates to stabilise.
In the bond market, the benchmark 10-year 86/4 bond yield fell to 6.1075 percent.
